skill.name: research-grants
skill.description: Draft and review research grant proposals for NSF, NIH, DOE, DARPA, and Taiwan NSTC programs. Includes agency guidance, proposal templates, budget justification support, broader impacts planning, and compliance reminders.
skill.summary: Prepare agency-specific research grant proposals, budgets, aims pages, and review-ready narratives.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by grant-writing prose, Markdown paths, and reference material. The remaining security concerns are a public git clone example and a mandatory Bash command for an unbundled script. No prompt injection, credential access, or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Mandatory Bash-based schematic generation uses an unbundled relative script.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the mandatory Bash step, bundle the script with the skill, or require explicit user confirmation before running it.

remediation.issue: Reference material includes a git clone command for a third-party repository.
remediation.suggestion: Label the command as manual setup only and instruct users to inspect the upstream repository before cloning it.

remediation.issue: The skill grants Bash access for a writing-focused workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Limit default tooling to document reads and edits unless a user explicitly requests local command execution.

content.value_statement: Research grant proposals require agency-specific structure, review criteria, budgets, and compliance details. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code draft focused proposal sections and review them against funder expectations.
actual_capabilities: Drafts proposal sections for NSF, NIH, DOE, DARPA, and Taiwan NSTC programs.
Structures NIH Specific Aims pages with gap, hypothesis, aims, innovation, and impact elements.
Builds NSF project summaries with overview, intellectual merit, and broader impacts sections.
Prepares budget justification language for personnel, equipment, travel, supplies, and other costs.
Reviews proposal drafts against significance, innovation, feasibility, milestones, and compliance expectations.
Compares agency expectations, page limits, review criteria, and submission planning needs.
limitations: It does not replace official solicitation instructions or institutional sponsored research review.
It cannot verify current deadlines, forms, or funding opportunity changes without fresh source checking.
It provides writing support, not legal, financial, or compliance approval for submissions.
It cannot guarantee funding outcomes or reviewer scores.

use_cases.title: Prepare an NSF Submission
use_cases.description: Create a project summary, broader impacts plan, and project description outline aligned with NSF merit review criteria.

use_cases.title: Refine NIH Specific Aims
use_cases.description: Turn a research idea into a one-page aims structure with significance, innovation, approach, and expected impact.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Proposal Package
use_cases.description: Draft budget justification text, timeline language, compliance reminders, and internal review checklists for a proposal team.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Proposal Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me outline a grant proposal for [agency] about [research topic]. Include required sections, reviewer priorities, and questions for me.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Specific Aims
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an NIH Specific Aims page for [project]. Use this hypothesis, these aims, and this expected impact: [details].

prompt_templates.title: Improve Broader Impacts
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this NSF broader impacts plan. Make activities specific, measurable, feasible, and connected to the research: [paste plan].

prompt_templates.title: Audit Proposal Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this [agency and mechanism] draft from a grant reviewer perspective. Identify weaknesses in significance, innovation, approach, team, budget, timeline, and compliance.

output_examples.input: Draft an NSF project summary for a climate data science proposal.
output_examples.output: A one-page summary organized into Overview, Intellectual Merit, and Broader Impacts, with clear research goals and measurable outreach activities.

output_examples.input: Review my NIH Specific Aims page for clarity and impact.
output_examples.output: A reviewer-style critique covering the opening hook, gap statement, central hypothesis, aim logic, innovation, feasibility, and final impact statement.

output_examples.input: Create a budget justification for a three-year DOE project.
output_examples.output: Narrative justification for personnel, fringe, equipment, travel, materials, publication costs, and indirect costs tied to project tasks.

best_practices: Start with the exact solicitation, agency rules, page limits, and review criteria before drafting.
Provide concrete project details, team roles, preliminary data, budget assumptions, and deadline constraints.
Have a human expert and institutional office review all compliance, budget, and submission materials.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic proposal language that could fit any project or agency.
Do not treat broader impacts, milestones, or budget justification as last-minute attachments.
Do not submit AI-generated text without checking factual accuracy, eligibility, formatting, and sponsor rules.

faq.question: Which funders does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers NSF, NIH, DOE, DARPA, and Taiwan NSTC guidance included in the skill references.

faq.question: Can it write a full proposal?
faq.answer: It can draft sections and outlines, but you must provide project details and perform expert review.

faq.question: Does it check current deadlines?
faq.answer: No. Verify deadlines, forms, and requirements against the current solicitation and official portals.

faq.question: Can it help with budgets?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft budget justification language and explain common budget categories.

faq.question: Is it suitable for resubmissions?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for responding to reviewer comments and strengthening revised narratives.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the agency, mechanism, solicitation, research aims, team roles, budget assumptions, timeline, and draft text.
